messages:
maya: FYI — noticed sample app README uses old client initialization, causing 401s when copying into a new node/ts app.

maya: Wrong snippet:
```js
// README (outdated)
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new RedwoodClient('TOKEN'); // old ctor, token should be in options
```

maya: New SDK uses default export and options object, plus async init for fetch-based auth:
```js
// Fix
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk').default;
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
await client.init(); // required in browser-ish runtimes
```

simon: ugh. Thanks — I hit this copying into a Codesandbox earlier. Can we keep both snippets (node + browser) and highlight need for await? :+1:

eli: +1. Also add note about retry behavior — browser fetch may throw if credentials unset, we got unhelpful stack traces.

maya: I'll open a small PR to update README and sample app. Planning to:
- replace single snippet with two labeled blocks
- add "if you see 401" troubleshooting paragraph
- add quick test script `npm run smoke` for sample-app

simon: ping @docs-bot for review and link to commit when done?

docs-bot: created PR #442: docs(devex): split SDK init snippets and add troubleshooting — https://git.internal/redwood/inference/pull/442 :white_check_mark:

eli: quick note — ensure the snippet uses `client.generate()` in examples not `client.completions()`; parity issue across SDKs caused more confusion.

maya: will update all occurrences. Also adding an inline comment about retry backoff defaults.

release-bot: docs published to staging at https://staging.docs.redwood.ai/quickstart  (build 2026-03-24T08:12Z)

simon: thanks! leaving a TODO on the sample app readme to add a tiny e2e script later.
